newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds keep wary eye on Treasuries, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds keep wary eye on Treasuries, Brazil.

text.p: The Brady bond market remained weak on Wednesday, with dealers looking for direction in U.S. Treasury notes and waiting to see where Brazil's domestic markets would trade.
On Tuesday the market suffered sharp declines amid growing concern that recent currency turmoil in Asia and Eastern Europe might spill over into Brazil.
Fears that Brazil might be forced to devalue shook local stock markets, and debt prices fell too.
"The major Latin American countries are up about 1/8 point from New York close, but it has been street buying rather than market buying," a dealer at a U.S. bank said.
"We will be waiting to see where the U.S. Treasury bond goes and how Brazil local markets open up this morning," he said.
Benchmark Brazilian "C" bonds were trading at 81.125 bid at 1145 GMT, up a quarter point from New York's close.
European debt has been hit too. Bulgaria in particular traded lower on Wednesday, with its "IAB" bonds at 73.375 bid, 1/8 point lower on the New York close.

"Bulgaria is quite illiquid and has been hit by supply," a debt trader said. "The rest of the market has lost 30 to 50 basis points, and Bulgaria is just one of them. There is no special reason for the loss."
The winner during the Wednesday European session was Russia, with strong buying reported from domestic investors. All its debt was up, with the rise ranging between an 1/8 and 3/4 point.
"Overall, we are probably unchanged on the spread from New York's close but have traded low prices," a dealer said.
"The market is taking stock, and looking for direction," he said.
U.S. Treasuries in London remained steady, awaiting data to provide an excuse to push higher, dealers said.
At 1230 GMT the June consumer price index (CPI) is due, and industrial production and capacity utilisation at 1315 GMT. All are expected to point to a soft economy.
Meanwhile, sentiment in the primary market was so shaky after the recent market falls that Argentina decided to delay its planned $750 million global bond until volatility declined.
